# Introduction

As the Executive Director of the Green Transit Alliance (GTA), this project examines the environmental performance of public transportation agencies across the United States to identify those that stand out and those with room for improvement. To conduct this analysis, we combine data from the National Transit Database (NTD Service & Energy) and the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). These sources provide information on passenger trips, passenger miles, energy consumption, and estimated carbon dioxide emissions. After exploring and gathering data, our findings ultimately lead to the presentation of two awards: the Greenest Transit Agency Award and the Biggest Polluter Award.


# Data Acquisition

## State Electricity Profiles
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "Show Import Code"
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false
library(tidyverse)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(fs)
library(gt)
  
  

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
  
  dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
  
  fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
    BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
    RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
      req_url_path("electricity", 
                   "state", 
                   state_formatted) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>   
      req_retry(
        max_tries = 4, 
      ) |>
      req_perform(file_name)
    
    resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
  }
  
  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
    html_element("table") |> 
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
  
  if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
    TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }
  
  CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |> 
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
    pull(Rank)
  
  RATE <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    as.numeric()
  
  GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
             primary_source        = PRIMARY,
             electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
             # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
             generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
             state                 = state, 
             abbreviation          = abbr
  )
}
EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```


## NTD Energy Consumption
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "Show Import Code"
#| message: false
#| warning: false 
#| output: false
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)
  
  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
    
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }
  
  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }
  
  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

## NTD Service Data
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "Show Import Code"
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false

  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)
  
  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
    
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }
  
  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

# Data Exploration

## EIA State Electricity Profiles

#### Which 5 states have the most expensive retail electricity?
```{r}

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh),
    y = electricity_price_MWh,
    fill = electricity_price_MWh
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0("$", round(electricity_price_MWh, 1))),
    hjust = -0.15,
    color = "white",
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#287B8A",
    high = "#A4F2C6"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 450),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, 100)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 Electricity Prices by State (2025)",
    x = "State",
    y = "Electricity Cost (USD per MWh)",
  caption = "Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), State Energy Profiles (2025)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#172A35", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#172A35", color = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "white", face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#C0D1D8", size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "white"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "white"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#38505A"),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#C0D1D8",size = 10,hjust = 0,margin = margin(t = 15)),
    plot.caption.position = "plot")
```
Based on the graph, we can see that Hawaii has the highest retail electricity price at $380 per MWh. The second most expensive taste, California, had a electricity cost of $270.4 per MWh. Meanwhile, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts have relatively similar electricity prices, ranging from $239.40 to $243.70 per MWh.

#### Which 5 states have the ‘dirtiest’ electricity mix?
```{r}

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(CO2_MWh, n = 5) |>
  select(state, CO2_MWh, primary_source) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Five States with the Dirtiest Electricity Mix",
    subtitle = "Carbon dioxide emissions per megawatt-hour"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    state = "State",
    CO2_MWh = "CO₂ Emissions (lbs/MWh)" ,
    primary_source = "Primary Energy Source"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = CO2_MWh,
    decimals = 0
  )|>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note=("Source: The EIA SEP Report"))|>
  tab_options(
  heading.background.color = "#0D0D0D",
  column_labels.background.color = "#287B8A",
  table.width = pct(85),
  table.align = "center",
  row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE,
  quarto.disable_processing = TRUE
)|>
  tab_style(
  style = cell_fill(color = "white"),
  locations = cells_body()
)|>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#C0D1D8"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "subtitle")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
  style = list(
    cell_fill(color = "#F0F0F0"),
    cell_text(
      color = "#444444",
      size = px(15),
      weight = "normal"
    )
  ),
  locations = cells_source_notes()
)
```
In this analysis, a dirtier electricity mix refers to higher amounts of CO2 emitted per Mwh. As shown by the table West Virginia takes first place in having the dirtiest electricity mix, producing 1,912 pounds of CO2 per MWh. An important thing to note is that four of the five states rely primarily on coal for electricity generation, while Hawaii is the only state on the list that relies primarily on petroleum.

```{r}
)|>

  style = list(
    cell_fill(color = "#F0F0F0"),

      color = "#444444",
      size = px(15),
      weight = "normal"
    )
  ),
  locations = cells_source_notes()
)

```
The 3 rarest primary energy sources are Hydroelectric (used in 4 states), Petroleum (used in 1 state), and Wind (used in 4 states). Currently, Vermont has the most expensive Hydroelectric electrcity price in the country at $184.10 per MWH. When, moving onto Wind, we can see that Kansas takes the lead at $112.1 per MWH. Lastly, Hawaii is the only state that primarily relies on petroleum, with a significantly higher electricity price of $380.00 per MWh.


#### How many times cleaner is NY’s energy mix than that of Texas?
```{r}
ratio<- EIA_SEP_REPORT|>
  filter(state=="New York" | state=="Texas")|>
  select(state,CO2_MWh)|>
  summarise(times_cleaner=CO2_MWh[state=="Texas"]/
            CO2_MWh[state=="New York"])|>
  pull(times_cleaner)
```
NY's energy mix is  `r round(ratio,2)` times cleaner than that of Texas.

## Transit Energy Usage
#### Across all US public transit, visualize the amounts of each type of fuel used
```{r}


NTD_FUEL<-NTD_ENERGY |>
  select(starts_with("Gallons of")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "fuel_source",
    values_to = "gallons"
  ) |>
  group_by(fuel_source) |>
  summarise(total_gallons = sum(gallons))|>
  mutate(fuel_source = str_remove(fuel_source, "Gallons of ")) |>
  arrange(desc(total_gallons))



ggplot(NTD_FUEL,
       aes(x = reorder(fuel_source, total_gallons),
           y = total_gallons,

  geom_col() +

    plot.title = element_text(color = "white", size = 20, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#C0D1D8", size = 13),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "white", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "white", size = 14),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(
    color = "#C0D1D8",
    size = 10,
    hjust = 0,
    margin = margin(t = 15)
    ),
    plot.caption.position = "plot")
    
```
As seen on the bar graph above, Diesel Fuel looks to be the most used fuel type at 437.9 million gallons, followed by compressed natural gas at 198.8 million and gasoline at 99.9 million. Another important thing to take note of is that kerosene and bunker fuel have no reported usage in the data set.

#### What is the least commonly used fuel source for US public transit?
```{r}

Least_used_fuel<- NTD_ENERGY |>
  select(
    starts_with("Gallons of"),
    starts_with("Kilowatt hours"),
    starts_with("Kilograms of")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "fuel_source",
    values_to = "consumption"
  ) |>
  group_by(fuel_source) |>
  summarise(
    number_of_records = sum(consumption > 0))|>
  arrange(number_of_records)|>
  filter(number_of_records>0)|>
  slice_min(number_of_records,n=1)|>
  mutate(fuel_source=str_remove(fuel_source,"Gallons of"))|>
  pull(fuel_source)

```
The least commonly used fuel source for US public transit was `r Least_used_fuel`.

## Transit Service 

#### What is the average trip length of a trip on MTA NYC?
```{r}
ATL<-NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(AGENCY == "MTA New York City Transit") |>
  summarise(
    average_trip_length = sum(sum_passenger_miles) /
      sum(total_upt)
  )|>
  pull(average_trip_length)

```
The average trip length of a trip on MTA NYC is `r round(ATL,2)` miles.

#### Are all states represented in this data? 
```{r}

NUMBER_OF_STATES<-NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(state %in% state.abb) |>
  summarise(total = n_distinct(state)) |>
  pull(total)
```
All `r NUMBER_OF_STATES` are represented in this data

# Agency Emissions and Efficency Analysis

## Total Carbon Dioxide Emissions
```{R}

ENERGY_CLEAN <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = str_pad(`NTD ID`, width = 5, pad = "0"))


SERVICE_CLEAN <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  select(NTD_ID, mode,state) |>
  distinct()



TRANSIT_DATA <- ENERGY_CLEAN |>
  inner_join(
    SERVICE_CLEAN,
    by = join_by(NTD_ID, Mode == mode),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )




EMISSIONS_DATA <- TRANSIT_DATA |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
    by = join_by(state == abbreviation),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
Final_Table <- EMISSIONS_DATA |>
  mutate(
    # Electricity
    electric_kWh = `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`,

    electric_emissions = case_when(
      electric_kWh == 0 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ electric_kWh / 1000 * CO2_MWh
    ),

    # Diesel and gasoline
    diesel_emissions = `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 22.45,
    gasoline_emissions = `Gallons of Gasoline` * 18.73,

    # Other petroleum fuels
    kerosene_emissions = `Gallons of Kerosene` * 21.78,
    bunker_emissions = `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * 24.78,
    lpg_emissions = `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 12.68,

    # Biofuels (approximated using diesel/gasoline) and LNG
    biodiesel_emissions = `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 22.45,
    ethanol_emissions = `Gallons of Ethanol` * 18.73,
    lng_emissions = `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * 9.25,

    # Compressed natural gas and hydrogen
    cng_emissions = `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 14.02,
    hydrogen_emissions = `Kilograms of Hydrogen` * 0,

    # Total CO2 emissions
    total_emissions = electric_emissions +
      diesel_emissions +
      gasoline_emissions +
      kerosene_emissions +
      bunker_emissions +
      lpg_emissions +
      biodiesel_emissions +
      ethanol_emissions +
      lng_emissions +
      cng_emissions +
      hydrogen_emissions
  )
(Color_Table<- Final_Table |>
  filter(!is.na(total_emissions)) |>
  slice_max(total_emissions, n = 10) |>
  select(`Agency Name`, Mode, state, total_emissions) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = " Top 10 Transit Operations by Total CO2 Emissions"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name` = "Transit Agency",
    Mode = "Mode",
    state = "State",
    total_emissions = "CO₂ Emissions (Million lbs)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
  columns = total_emissions,
  scale_by = 1/1000000,
  decimals = 2
)|>
  tab_source_note(
  source_note = "Source: NTD Service, NTD Energy, and EIA SEP Report"
) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Calculations based on EIA emissions coefficients and approximations"
  ) |>
    tab_options(
  heading.background.color = "#0D0D0D",
  column_labels.background.color = "#287B8A",
  table.width = pct(85),
  table.align = "center",
  row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE,
  quarto.disable_processing = TRUE
)|>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#C0D1D8"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "subtitle")
  ) |>
    tab_style(
  style = list(
    cell_fill(color = "#F0F0F0"),
    cell_text(
      color = "#444444",
      size = px(13),
      weight = "normal"
    )
  ),
  locations = cells_source_notes()
))

```
To estimate the total CO2 emissions associated with public transit systems across the United States, I obtained the coefficients from the EIA website, specifically looking at the pounds of CO2 columns. Where I then proceeeded to multipliy each fuel's consumption by its respective coefficient. Certain fuel sources did not have an exact match in the EIA report, so I used a reasonable approximation. Its important to note that four agency mode combinations could not be assigned complete emissions estimates because electricity emissions rates were unavailable for Washington, DC, and Puerto Rico. Moving onto the table above we can see that MTA New York City Transit occupies the top two positions, with Heavy Rail generating approximately 900.41 million pounds of CO2 and Motor Bus accounting for 663.04 million pounds. Another key thing to note is that four of the ten highest total emmissions combinationsare located in New York. This goes to show the amount of public transportation needed in big cities.



## Emissions per Passenger Trip

```{r}
# Calculate emissions for each agency

AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- Final_Table|>
  group_by(NTD_ID, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarise(
    total_CO2 = sum(total_emissions),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate total passenger usage for each agency
AGENCY_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarise(
    total_trips = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join datasets and calculate emissions efficiency
AGENCY_EFFICIENCY <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  inner_join(
    AGENCY_SERVICE,
    by = "NTD_ID",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    CO2_per_UPT = if_else(
      total_trips > 0,
      total_CO2 / total_trips,
      NA_real_
    ),
    CO2_per_mile = if_else(
      passenger_miles > 0,
      total_CO2 / passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    ),
    agency_size = case_when(
      total_trips < 500000 ~ "Small",
      total_trips < 5000000 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "Large"
    )
  )

# Five most efficient agencies per size category
TOP_UPT <- AGENCY_EFFICIENCY |>
  filter(!is.na(CO2_per_UPT)) |>
  group_by(agency_size) |>
  slice_min(CO2_per_UPT, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()





TOP_UPT |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    agency_size,
    total_trips,
    CO2_per_UPT
  ) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "agency_size") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Most Efficient Transit Agencies by Passenger Trip",
    subtitle = "Five lowest-emitting agencies in each size category"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name` = "Transit Agency",
    total_trips = "Annual Passenger Trips (Millions)",
    CO2_per_UPT = "CO₂ (lbs/trip)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = total_trips,
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
  columns = total_trips,
  scale_by = 1/1000000,
  decimals = 2
) |>
   fmt_number(
    columns = CO2_per_UPT,
    decimals = 2
   )|>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Sources: NTD Service, NTD Energy, and EIA SEP Report"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Small: <500K trips | Medium: 500K–5M | Large: 5M+"
  ) |>
  tab_options(
  heading.background.color = "#0D0D0D",
  column_labels.background.color = "#287B8A",
  table.width = pct(85),
  table.align = "center",
  row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE,
  quarto.disable_processing = TRUE
)|>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#C0D1D8"),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "subtitle")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "#287B8A", weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_source_notes()
  )|>
  tab_style(
  style = list(
    cell_fill(color = "#F0F0F0"),
    cell_text(
      color = "#444444",
      size = px(15),
      weight = "normal"
    )
  ),
  locations = cells_source_notes()
)
```
To compare transit agencies more fairly, I divided the 522 agencies from the Emissions data (previous table) into small, medium, and large categories based on the annual passenger trips. Among large agencies, Anaheim Transportation Network recorded the lowest estimated emissions per passenger trip at 0.20 pounds of CO2, followed by the Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon at 0.40 pounds. For medium sized agencies, the City of Seattle led with just 0.06 pounds per trip, while the City of Milwaukee ranked first among small agencies at 0.32 pounds.

# Transit Agency Awards

## The Greenest Transit Agency Award goes to ...

The Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon  has earned the Greenest Transit Agency Award, recording the lowest estimated carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile among 217 eligible public transportation agencies. With approximately 270.79 million passenger miles annually, the  Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation of Oregon generated an estimated 26.28 million pounds of CO2, equivalent to **0.097 pounds per passenger mile**.

To figure out who the winner of this award,  each agency's estimated total CO2 emissions was divided by its annual passenger miles. And to be qualify for this award, Agencies were required to be U.S. only agencies, have at least 500,000 annual passenger trips and 10 million passenger miles. After gathering all the eligible agencies, the median came out to be  0.814 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. So, when comparing the winner of this award to the median, it outperformed greatly as their **estimated emissions per passenger mile  was 88.1% lower than the median**. These results demonstrate that large scale public transportation can achieve low emissions per passenger mile.

## The Biggest Polluter Award goes to...
This year's Planet's Biggest Polluter Award goes to the Port Imperial Ferry Corporation, which recorded the highest estimated carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile among 217 eligible agencies. This award uses the same eligibility as the Greenest Transit Agency award, this allows it to be fair to all agencies.  Port Imperial Ferry Corporation generated approximately 3.1 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile, compared with the median 0.840 pounds. This places its estimated emissions intensity at  **3.8 times the median**. It’s also important to note that several other ferry operators appear among the highest emitting agencies, suggesting that this mode of transportation may face challenges in reducing emissions per passenger mile.

```{r}
      margin = margin(t = 15)
    ),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(20, 25, 20, 20)
  )

WORST_PLOT
```



::: {.callout-note title="AI Usage Statement" collapse="true"}

ChatGPT was used to assist with R code, including data acquisition, table formatting, and website design. It was also used to troubleshoot errors. The analysis, interpretation of tables, and the press release were written by me.

:::
